raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Purpose

Remove HiSparse-specific overrides and special cases from general KV-cache paths, and dedupe the scheduler's load-start code. No intended behavior change for HiSparse; one small zeroing change for copy-on-write blocks, described below.

| Change | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Deferred-load start | `_drain_deferred_loads` repeats `update_state_after_alloc` and the prefix-stats recording from `schedule()` | both call `_update_connector_after_alloc` |
| Host block ids in GPU zeroing | `HiSparseSourceManager` overrides `records_new_block_ids` and `take_new_block_ids` to discard host ids after they are recorded | `bind_host_pool` clears `_record_new_block_ids`; the base copy-on-write path now honors that flag (it appended unconditionally) |
| Hot-page stride alignment | `_get_kv_cache_bytes_per_block` special-cases `isinstance(spec, HiSparseHotSpec)` | `HiSparseHotSpec.get_block_stride_alignment()` includes its page size |

Why each is equivalent:
- **Deferred-load start:** the deferral condition, the fence stamp and the drain loop are unchanged, and each load still starts before its stats are recorded.
- **Copy-on-write guard:** CoW blocks now follow the same per-manager `_record_new_block_ids` rule as every other allocation path. For HiSparse host this is what the removed overrides did. **Behavior change:** with zeroing on, a base-path CoW block in a manager that doesn't record new blocks (circular buffer, non-`AttentionSpec` specs) is no longer zeroed. Its regular blocks already weren't. Mamba has its own CoW path and is unaffected.
- **Alignment:** hot groups always carry per-layer names that share the spec, so the hot page size still enters the LCM. On the layer-outermost path, rounding a page up to itself is a no-op.

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest tests/v1/core/test_deferred_block_free.py tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py \
  tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_planning.py \
  tests/v1/core/test_contiguous_kv_packing.py tests/v1/core/test_single_type_kv_cache_manager.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_hisparse_connector.py tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_multi_connector.py
```

New coverage, confirmed to fail when the code it guards is reverted:
- `test_hisparse_host_cow_copy_is_drained_without_a_gpu_pool` runs with zeroing on (dropping the CoW guard or the `bind_host_pool` flag clear fails it).

## Test Result

- **macOS (CPU), head cc5f1e045b:** all the listed suites pass, except 11 failures in `test_scheduler.py` (diffusion) and `test_hisparse_connector.py::test_draft_layer_rows_mirrored_after_drafter`. The same 11 fail at the PR head before the review commits.
- **GPU (4x B200, CUDA 13.0), PR be49e2c334 vs `main` dc45a5f552:** later commits only add a test and a docstring, restore the original async-load deferral gate, change the alignment to an LCM (same value unless a hot spec sets `block_stride_alignment`), and merge `main`.
  - **Unit tests:** `pytest tests/v1/core/test_deferred_block_free.py tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_hisparse_connector.py tests/v1/attention/test_sparse_mla_backends.py -k "hisparse or test_deferred_block_free"`: 88 passed. `pytest tests/v1/e2e/general/test_hisparse.py`: 5 passed.
  - **Forced host offload, async scheduling:** `vllm serve GLM-5.3-NVFP4 -tp 4 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --block-size 64 --max-model-len 24576 --max-num-seqs 64 --num-gpu-blocks-override 12000 --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"HiSparseConnector","kv_role":"kv_both","kv_connector_extra_config":{"host_pool_gib":64}}'`. GPU + host capacity is 31,561 tokens against ~108k tokens of demand. `/metrics` on the PR shows 14.4M hot-buffer misses, 32.5 GB of H2D and 79.7k prefix-cache hit tokens, so the offload and prefix paths ran.
  - **Greedy outputs match** (temperature 0, `ignore_eos`) on three workloads: 6 prompts of 12k-20k tokens sent concurrently, the same sent sequentially, and 9 prompts over 3 shared prefixes. Where the PR differs from `main`, `main` also differs from itself across runs, at the same near-tie positions. Wall time is 58 s vs 56 s, with the same running/waiting progression.
